header.title: OpenAEC Docs
header.heroAlt: Folder with the architect's drawings in a sample project, with the fixed project folders and two manifests in the sidebar
header.label: Document management
header.tagline: Project folders, models and manifests neatly together, on your own server
header.desc: OpenAEC Docs is a concept for document management in construction projects. It puts an overview of projects, fixed folders and manifests on top of the files already in your Nextcloud.

meta.description: Concept for open-source document management in construction projects: projects, fixed project folders and manifests on top of your own Nextcloud, on your own server. Still in development.
meta.title: OpenAEC Docs — OpenAEC Foundation

projects.alt: Overview of six fictitious projects, including a primary school, a cycle bridge and a housing template, each with status and project folder
projects.title: All your projects in one overview
projects.desc: Each project appears as a card with a short description, its status and the Nextcloud folder that holds the files. Active projects, archived records and templates are easy to tell apart. One click takes you into the project.

folders.alt: Project folder of a fictitious primary school with the fixed folders models, drawings, calculations, reports, permits and correspondence
folders.title: The same recognisable layout in every project
folders.desc: The sidebar shows the project's fixed folders, such as models, drawings, calculations and reports, with readable names. Everyone finds the right place straight away in every project, including newcomers.

models.alt: Folder with IFC models from the architect, structural engineer and building services engineers, with file sizes and the breadcrumb at the top
models.title: Your files stay where they already are
models.desc: OpenAEC Docs reads the files straight from your Nextcloud. You browse models, drawings and subfolders, see the size of every file and jump back through the breadcrumb. No second storage or copy is added.

manifest.alt: Manifest of a sample project with four IFC models, an issue set and a validation report, each with path and GUID
manifest.title: Record what belongs together
manifest.desc: A manifest in the project folder records which models, issue sets and reports belong to the project, each with a fixed key. OpenAEC Docs shows its contents clearly, and other tools can add items to it through the API.

notice.text: Concept: there is no version to install or try online yet, and development has been paused since April 2026. The screenshots come from a local test setup with fictitious projects.

overview.title: Project overview
overview.desc: All your organisation's projects as cards, with description and project folder.

status.title: Active, archived or template
status.desc: Every project has a status, so ongoing work, closed records and templates do not get mixed up.

projectapi.title: Create and archive projects
projectapi.desc: You link a project to a Nextcloud folder. Creating, editing and archiving work through the API for now, not yet on screen.

fixed.title: Fixed project folders
fixed.desc: A fixed layout per project in the sidebar, such as models, drawings and reports, in a fixed order.

browse.title: Browse with a breadcrumb
browse.desc: Browse folders and subfolders, folders first, with the size of every file and one click back.

nextcloud.title: Straight from Nextcloud
nextcloud.desc: The files stay in Nextcloud. OpenAEC Docs only stores the project details and the folder layout.

folderset.title: Settings per folder
folderset.desc: For each folder you record a name, order, icon, read-only and the file types that belong in it.

suggest.title: Suggest a layout
suggest.desc: OpenAEC Docs suggests the fixed folders from the folders that already exist: 01_Modellen becomes Modellen.

fileapi.title: Upload, delete, create folders
fileapi.desc: Fetch, upload and delete files and create folders in the project folder, through the API for now.

manifests.title: View manifests
manifests.desc: A manifest's header and items shown clearly: type, name, path and key.

multi.title: Several manifests per project
multi.desc: For example one for the models and one for the reports, each opened straight from the sidebar.

upsert.title: Add items
upsert.desc: Other tools add or update an item in a manifest through the API, matched on its fixed key.

api.title: Connect your own tools
api.desc: Projects, folders, files and manifests are all available through a single API.

selfhost.title: On your own server
selfhost.desc: Runs in Docker on a server you manage yourself. Your project data does not go to an outside cloud.

sso.title: Single sign-on
sso.desc: Sign in through your organisation's sign-in server, without a separate password for OpenAEC Docs.

tenants.title: Several organisations
tenants.desc: One installation for several organisations, each with its own Nextcloud and only access to its own projects.

features.label: Features
features.heading: What OpenAEC Docs can do now
features.sub: Start with the highlights, or pick a topic.

multi.title: Several manifests
multi.desc: Every manifest file in the project folder appears separately in the sidebar.

viewer.title: Manifest on screen
viewer.desc: A manifest's header and items, with type, name, path and key.

upsert.title: Add through the API
upsert.desc: Other tools add or update items; if the manifest does not exist yet, it is created.

shared.title: Same format as other tools
shared.desc: The manifest uses the shared library of the OpenAEC cloud tools, so they can read it too.

whatsnew.label: New in April 2026
whatsnew.title: Manifests: what belongs with what
whatsnew.desc: The latest new feature dates from April 2026: a project can have several manifests, which you view on screen. Development has been paused since then; there is no release yet.

files.a: OpenAEC Docs shows every file in the project folder in Nextcloud, from IFC models to PDF and DWG drawings, with name and size. You can read manifests (.wefc) on screen. Opening a file or showing a preview is not yet possible on screen; through the API you can fetch any file.

install.q: Do I need to install anything?
install.a: Yes. OpenAEC Docs is a server application you run in Docker on your own server, together with PostgreSQL, a Nextcloud for the files and a sign-in server. Users then work in the browser. There is no ready-made release and no public trial version yet.

price.a: Nothing. OpenAEC Docs is open source under the MIT licence. You only pay for your own server.

format.q: In which file format is my work saved?
format.a: Your files stay unchanged in Nextcloud. The project details and folder layout are kept in a PostgreSQL database, and manifests are .wefc files (JSON) in the project folder.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: The server runs in Docker, on Linux. Users work in a modern browser on Windows, macOS or Linux.

practice.a: It follows common practice: a fixed folder structure per project, IFC models per discipline and manifests that keep models, issue sets (BCF) and reports together. Links with the BIM Validator and the BCF platform are prepared but do not work yet.

ai.q: What can an AI assistant do with it?
ai.a: There is no MCP server yet. An assistant or script can, however, use the REST API to read projects, folders, files and manifests and add items to a manifest.

status.a: Not for real work yet. OpenAEC Docs is a concept: the basis is in place, but there is no release, no public installation and no new development since April 2026. If you want to help, have a look at the source code on GitHub.

buttons.q: Can I upload and create folders on screen?
buttons.a: Not yet. The buttons for upload, new folder, search and document status are already in the ribbon but do nothing yet. Uploading, deleting and creating folders do work through the API.

nextcloud.a: Yes. OpenAEC Docs has no file storage of its own; it works with the files in your organisation's Nextcloud. For each organisation you set which Nextcloud belongs to it.

rust.desc: A fast, compact server in Rust with Axum that passes all requests on to Nextcloud.

react.desc: The web interface in React 19 and TypeScript, built with Vite and styled with Tailwind in the OpenAEC style.

nextcloud.desc: Files live in Nextcloud and are read and written over WebDAV; OpenAEC Docs stores no files itself.

postgres.desc: Projects, folder layout, users and roles in PostgreSQL, with SQLx and numbered migrations.

oidc.desc: Sign-in through OpenID Connect with PKCE (for example Authentik) and a session token valid for 24 hours.

docker.desc: A single image with server and web interface, plus Docker Compose files for development and production.

tech.heading: Technology
tech.sub: For those who want to know how it is built.
